title: Rational Functions and Asymptotes
domain: Cubic, Cube Root, Absolute Value, and Rational Functions, Equations, and Inequalities
standard_text: 2A.6G analyze the effect on the graphs of f(x) = 1/x when f(x) is replaced by af(x), f(bx), f(x − c), and f(x) + d for specific positive and negative real values of a, b, c, and d; 2A.6K determine the asymptotic restrictions on the domain of a rational function and represent domain and range using interval notation, inequalities, and set notation
meta_desc: Free Algebra II rational function worksheets for Texas TEKS 2A.6G and 2A.6K: transformations of 1/x, asymptotes, holes, domain and range in interval and set notation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: a/(x − c) + d: asymptotes x = c and y = d.
key_sub: Domain: x ≠ c. Range: y ≠ d.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • g(x) = ax − c + d has a vertical asymptote x = c and a horizontal asymptote y = d.
  • Domain: every x except c. Range: every y except d.
  • A factor that cancels from the top and bottom makes a hole, not an asymptote.
  • Horizontal asymptote: compare degrees. Bottom bigger → y = 0; equal → ratio of leading coefficients; top one bigger → slant asymptote.

Examples

Example

g(x) = 3x + 2 − 1

Left 2, down 1, stretch by 3

Answer: Asymptotes x = −2 and y = −1

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The wrong sign for the vertical asymptotex + 2 = 0 gives x = −2.
Swapping the asymptotesc is vertical (x = c), d is horizontal (y = d).
Calling a hole an asymptoteA factor that cancels makes a hole.

faq.a: Sometimes, for more complicated rational functions, but 1/x and its shifts never do.

faq.q: What does a negative a do?
faq.a: It reflects the graph over the x-axis.

items.e: (x − 3) cancels, so there is a hole at x = 3. The simplified function is 1/(x − 1); at x = 3 it is 12. The hole is (3, 12).
